basis: Renal sodium-retaining tubulopathy defined by hypertension and hypokalemia; cerebral ischemia is a secondary vascular complication.
Congenital limb skeletal malformation with absent digits, split hands/feet and syndactyly.
Constitutional 13q deletion syndromes commonly cause developmental delay and intellectual disability; other organ malformations vary substantially by deleted segment.
Cerebellar ataxia, developmental impairment and cerebellar atrophy define disease. Optic pallor in one assessed patient does not establish common ocular damage; nystagmus is neurologic.
Presenile dementia denotes loss of cerebral cognitive function; dementia is explicitly annotated.
Intracranial arterial stenosis defines moyamoya; intrinsic ischemic or hemorrhagic brain injury commonly exceeds 30% over its course, although ANO1-specific frequency is uncertain.
Epithelial neoplasm arising in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Primary CNS glial tumor composed of astrocytic and oligodendroglial elements.
GPI-anchor remodeling disorder with intellectual disability; retinal dystrophy 2/2 and pulmonic stenosis 1/2 assessed. Small samples; cap omits enamel hypoplasia 1/1.
Developmental impairment and hyperkinetic movement disorder define CNS disease; cardiomyopathy in 1/3 assessed (~33%), with substantial uncertainty from the small sample.
Mitochondrial/peroxisomal fission disorder causing encephalopathy; optic pallor and visual impairment in 3/4, with optic atrophy frequent. Weakness and dysphagia are neurologic manifestations.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration; nystagmus and abnormal pursuit reflect cerebellar dysfunction, while dysphagia does not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
Epilepsy with intellectual disability defines CNS involvement; nystagmus and facial dysmorphism do not establish damage to another organ axis.
Upper motor neuron degeneration causes spastic weakness and bulbar dysfunction; no evidence of primary muscle or gastrointestinal tissue disease.
Pure anxiety/phobic disorder without defined damage to an organ axis.
Most mesotheliomas arise in pleura; peritoneal and pericardial origins are minority subtypes and do not warrant additional axes for the umbrella.
Breast carcinoma classification; breast lies outside the organ axes, regardless of receptor expression.
Inherited connective tissue disorders predominantly affect the locomotor connective tissues; vascular, ocular and skin damage varies across this broad group.
Palmoplantar keratoderma/nail dystrophy and hereditary motor-sensory neuropathy are defining components.
Most small cell carcinomas originate in lung. Neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease; metastatic organ disease requires separate assessment.
Defined by proximal renal tubular dysfunction (Fanconi syndrome) and neonatal hyperinsulinism.
Severe mevalonate metabolism disorder with autoinflammation and neurodegeneration; cataracts in 3/3 assessed (nuclear 2/3). Four-axis cap omits myopathy and anemia (3/3).
Opportunistic fungal infection; pulmonary, bloodstream and cutaneous sites are variable examples, without evidence that any specific damaged organ occurs in at least 30%.
Relapsing inflammatory/autoimmune optic neuropathy; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis, and disease is explicitly isolated.
Testicular germ cell tumor lies outside the axes; hepatoid describes cell morphology and does not indicate hepatic disease or endocrine-gland origin.
